CHIEF COMPLAINT
Big toe pain and redness

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with approximately 2 weeks of intermittent pain in the big toe, with worsening and increased intensity over the past week. Pain became severe enough that patient was unable to walk at a trade show/convention last week and could only stand. Pain is described as throbbing in character with occasional sharp stabbing quality, particularly with movement or prolonged walking. Patient reports walking on heel to avoid bending the toe. Onset was not associated with any remembered injury. Patient became particularly concerned when the toe became red and warm to the touch. Pain is significantly worse with light pressure, including when bed sheets come in contact with the toe at night and when rolling over in bed. Current pain management with ibuprofen 2 tablets daily has been ineffective.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any history of stomach problems. Patient reports enjoying spicy foods without issue.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 2 tablets daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a job requiring standing on feet most of the day. Hobbies include cycling (reports riding over 800 miles in the past year on trails) and fishing. Typically wears flip-flops. Uses regular shoe on regular pedal for cycling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals redness and warmth of the big toe with visible bone spur on the dorsal aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Palpation of the first MTP joint reveals pain with range of motion testing. Dorsiflexion causes pain. Plantar flexion is restricted to approximately 10 degrees with pain, increasing to approximately 20 degrees with increased pain. Medial-lateral translation reproduces pain with grinding quality noted. Medial pressure between the big toe and second toe causes mild pain. Lateral pressure on the outside of the toe causes significant pain. Bone spur palpated on the dorsal aspect of the first MTP joint.

RESULTS
X-ray of the foot shows a large bone spur on the dorsal aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with significant cartilage loss.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus with first metatarsophalangeal joint osteoarthritis and osteophyte formation. Patient to begin orthotic shoe insert. Start meloxicam once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Patient counseled regarding potential gastrointestinal side effects including heartburn and epigastric pain; instructed to discontinue medication and contact office if such symptoms develop. Patient to continue regular work and activities to allow adequate assessment of treatment effectiveness. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. If significant improvement not achieved, will discuss more invasive options including corticosteroid injection, arthroscopic joint debridement, or first MTP joint fusion.
